fields.name: pve_api_host
fields.label: API host
fields.help: Host name or IP address of a Proxmox VE node (the API listens on it).

fields.name: pve_api_user
fields.label: API user
fields.help: The user that owns the token, user@realm.

fields.name: pve_api_token_id
fields.label: Token name
fields.help: The token's name only (automation, not ansible@pve!automation).

fields.name: pve_api_token_secret
fields.label: Token secret
fields.help: The token's secret, a UUID.

fields.name: pve_validate_certs
fields.label: Verify the API's TLS certificate
fields.help: Leave this on. For the node's self-signed certificate, add the cluster CA below instead.

fields.name: pve_node
fields.label: Node name
fields.help: The Proxmox node the VMs are created on, as Proxmox names it, unless a server names its own node on the Servers page. Proxmox node name.

fields.name: pve_storage
fields.label: VM disk storage
fields.help: Storage for the VM disks.

fields.name: pve_efidisk_format
fields.label: EFI disk format
fields.help: Raw for LVM/ZFS/Ceph, qcow2 for directory storage.

fields.name: pve_bridge
fields.label: Network bridge
fields.help: Bridge of the first network card, net0.

fields.name: pve_vlan
fields.label: VLAN tag
fields.help: VLAN tag of net0 (1-4094), empty for none.

fields.name: pve_iso_storage
fields.label: ISO storage
fields.help: A Proxmox storage that allows ISO images (Content: ISO image), such as local or an NFS share for the whole cluster. Its folder on the node is found automatically. The Proxmox storage for the ISOs (it must allow ISO images; a storage shared by the cluster, such as NFS, works for every node). Its folder on the node is asked from Proxmox (`pvesm path`); set pve_iso_dir only to override that, for an unusual setup.

fields.name: pve_api_timeout
fields.label: API request timeout (seconds)
fields.help: How long one Proxmox API request may take. Allocating disks can keep the API busy. Seconds Proxmox may take to answer one API request. Allocating disks (LVM-thin, ZFS, Ceph) can keep the API busy for longer than the Proxmox modules' own 5-second default.

fields.name: pve_ssh_user
fields.label: Node SSH user
fields.help: The UI and the playbooks log in to the node over SSH as this user. The user Ansible logs in to the Proxmox nodes as over SSH; the proxmox_nodes' ansible_user must match (the roles check). root needs nothing else. Any other user needs playbooks/prepare-node.yml run once (it logs in as root) first: it creates the user, with write access to the ISO storages' folders only (docs/installing.md).

fields.name: github_user
fields.label: GitHub user
fields.help: Whose public keys (https://github.com/<user>.keys) are installed for the admin user. Keys from https://github.com/<github_user>.keys plus any extras.

fields.name: github_keys_url
fields.label: Keys URL
fields.help: Where the keys come from. Leave the default unless you mirror them.

fields.name: admin_extra_ssh_keys
fields.label: Extra public keys
fields.help: One public key per line, installed besides the GitHub ones.

fields.name: admin_password
fields.label: Admin password
fields.help: For the console and sudo; SSH stays key-only. Hashed (SHA-512) before it reaches the installer.

fields.name: time_sync_servers
fields.label: Time servers (NTP)
fields.help: NTP servers the clock is set from, in place of the OS's own: host names or IP addresses. Empty, with no pools either, leaves the OS's own time sync as it is.

fields.name: time_sync_pools
fields.label: Time server pools (NTP)
fields.help: NTP pools: names that resolve to several servers. systemd-timesyncd, which has no pools, uses them as servers.

fields.name: vm_os
fields.label: Default OS
fields.help: For servers that don't choose their own on the Servers page. The server's operating system, from the OS catalog: ubuntu-26.04, debian-13, rocky-10 and so on (docs/interfaces.md lists them all). For all servers, or per server.

fields.name: vm_install_method
fields.label: Install method
fields.help: For servers that don't choose their own on the Servers page. A cloud image is imported as the VM's disk; it comes with the vendor's own disk layout. How the OS is installed: autoinstall, from the Ubuntu installer ISO (Ubuntu only; disk layouts and disk encryption need it), or cloud_image, from the vendor's cloud image (every release; the ISO storage must allow Import content).

fields.name: net_gateway
fields.label: Gateway
fields.help: Needed for servers with a static address (unless an extra network card has the default route).

fields.name: net_search
fields.label: Search domains
fields.help: Each part of a domain (between dots) must be a valid host name.

fields.name: autoinstall_storage_layout
fields.label: Disk layout
fields.help: For the Ubuntu installer; cloud images come with their own layout. Lvm, direct or zfs.

fields.name: vm_secure_boot
fields.label: Secure Boot keys
fields.help: Pre-enroll Microsoft's Secure Boot keys in the EFI disk, so the firmware boots only signed code (Ubuntu's shim, GRUB and kernel). New VMs only; set false for a VM that must boot unsigned kernels or modules.

fields.name: vm_disk_encryption
fields.label: Encrypt the root disk
fields.help: Only for VMs created from now on; existing VMs are left as they are. Encrypt the root disk with LUKS2 and unlock it at boot with a virtual TPM (Proxmox vTPM). The TPM releases the key only while Secure Boot state (PCR 7) is unchanged, so this needs vm_secure_boot and the lvm layout. It protects a copied disk image or backup, not a VM whose Proxmox host is compromised: see docs/security.md.

fields.name: vm_disk_passphrase
fields.label: Disk passphrase
fields.help: The recovery key: typed at the VM's console when the TPM doesn't unlock the disk. 12 to 512 printable ASCII characters, no braces. Kept in the Vault and never shown again, so keep a copy in your password manager. A new one applies to VMs created after it; existing VMs keep theirs.

fields.name: ssh_port
fields.label: SSH port
fields.help: Anything other than 22 switches sshd from ssh.socket to ssh.service; the firewall rule moves too.

fields.name: ssh_allow_users
fields.label: Allowed SSH users
fields.help: Empty allows every user. If set, it must include the admin user. Limit who may log in over SSH. Empty means no AllowUsers line. Keep admin_user in it.

fields.name: admin_sudo_nopasswd
fields.label: Passwordless sudo for the admin user
fields.help: Off by default: the first run removes the installer's passwordless sudo, and later runs use the admin password. On is convenient, but anyone with an authorized key has root. The installer grants passwordless sudo so the first baseline run can work unattended; with false (the default) that run removes it again, and later runs use ansible_become_password (the admin password).

fields.name: firewall_ssh_limit
fields.label: Rate-limit SSH in the firewall
fields.help: Rate-limit SSH (UFW's "limit": 6 connections in 30 s per source) instead of a plain allow.

fields.name: firewall_ssh_sources
fields.label: SSH allowed from
fields.help: "any", or addresses and networks (CIDR), one per line. Where SSH is allowed from. "any", or a list of addresses/CIDRs.

fields.name: firewall_allow
fields.label: Extra firewall rules (all servers)
fields.help: One rule per line: port or range, optional /tcp or /udp, optional "from" a network. Example: 443/tcp or 5432/tcp from 10.0.0.0/24. Extra rules, e.g.

fields.name: firewall_docker_enabled
fields.label: Apply the firewall to Docker-published ports
fields.help: Docker opens a container's published ports to everyone, past the firewall. On, only the sources and ports below reach them. Ubuntu and Debian only; servers without Docker are skipped. Docker-published ports. Docker forwards a published port (docker run -p, ports: in Compose) to its container through its own DOCKER-USER chain, before UFW's rules, so the port is open to everyone whatever UFW says. On, /etc/ufw/after.rules and after6.rules fill that chain: new connections to a published port are dropped unless they come from firewall_docker_sources or match firewall_docker_allow. Replies, and connections the containers make themselves, aren't affected. Skipped, with a message, on a server without Docker (run the baseline again after installing it). Not available on the RHEL family (firewalld) yet: the run stops there instead.

fields.name: firewall_docker_sources
fields.label: Docker ports allowed from
fields.help: Addresses or networks (CIDR) that may reach every published port, one per line. Addresses or networks (IPv4 or IPv6, CIDR) that may reach every published port.

fields.name: firewall_docker_allow
fields.label: Docker ports open
fields.help: One rule per line, with the port on the server (8080 in -p 8080:80): port or range, optional /tcp or /udp, optional "from" a network. Example: 8080/tcp or 9000:9010/udp from 10.0.0.0/24. Published ports open to everyone, or to one network: the port on the server (8080 in -p 8080:80), or a range, e.g.

fields.name: fail2ban_ignoreip
fields.label: Never ban
fields.help: Your own management networks, so a typo can't lock you out. Never ban these (add your admin networks so a typo can't lock you out).

fields.name: fail2ban_bantime_increment
fields.label: Longer bans for repeat offenders
fields.help: Each repeat offence bans longer, up to fail2ban_bantime_maxtime.

fields.name: fail2ban_sshd_mode
fields.label: sshd filter mode
fields.help: Normal, ddos, extra or aggressive.

fields.name: fail2ban_banaction
fields.label: Ban action
fields.help: Empty keeps Ubuntu's default (nftables).

fields.name: hardening_sysctl_enabled
fields.label: Kernel and network settings (sysctl)
fields.help: Write hardening_sysctl (plus hardening_sysctl_extra) to /etc/sysctl.d/90-usas-hardening.conf and apply it.

fields.name: hardening_auditd_enabled
fields.label: Audit changes with auditd
fields.help: Install auditd and load rules that watch identity files, sudoers, the sshd configuration, time changes, kernel module loading and the audit configuration and logs.

fields.name: hardening_auditd_immutable
fields.label: Lock the audit rules until a reboot
fields.help: Lock the rules until the next reboot (-e 2): nobody, root included, can change or stop auditing; changing the rules then needs a reboot.

fields.name: hardening_apparmor_enabled
fields.label: Keep AppArmor on and report profiles in complain mode
fields.help: Install AppArmor, keep it enabled and running so Ubuntu's profiles are loaded, and report profiles that are in complain mode (it doesn't change any profile's mode).

fields.name: unattended_upgrades_mail
fields.label: Mail update reports to
fields.help: Mail unattended-upgrades' report to this address (empty: no mail). Sending needs a mail transfer agent on the server: an existing one, or the msmtp relay below.

fields.name: unattended_upgrades_mail_report
fields.label: Which update reports
fields.help: Always, only-on-error or on-change.

fields.name: fail2ban_destemail
fields.label: Mail bans to
fields.help: Mail every ban, with a whois report of the address, to this address (Fail2Ban's action_mw). Needs a mail transfer agent on the server, such as the common role's msmtp relay (mail_relay_enabled).

fields.name: fail2ban_sender
fields.label: Ban mail sender
fields.help: The sender address; empty keeps Fail2Ban's default (root@<host>). The msmtp relay sends from mail_relay_from.

fields.name: fail2ban_webhook_url
fields.label: Webhook for bans
fields.help: An ntfy, Gotify, Slack, Discord or Mattermost URL that gets a message for every ban. It often holds a token, so it is kept in the Vault.

fields.name: fail2ban_webhook_format
fields.label: Webhook message format
fields.help: Text sends the message as the body (ntfy); json sends {"title", "text", "message", "content"} (Slack, Mattermost, Gotify, Discord).

fields.name: mail_relay_enabled
fields.label: Send mail through a relay (msmtp)
fields.help: Install msmtp-mta as the server's sendmail, passing all mail to mail_relay_host. It replaces no other mail server: the run stops if one (Postfix, Exim...) is installed.

fields.name: mail_relay_tls
fields.label: Relay encryption
fields.help: Starttls, tls (implicit TLS, usually port 465) or "off".

fields.name: mail_relay_from
fields.label: Sender address
fields.help: The sender address of the mail the server sends.

fields.name: mail_relay_user
fields.label: Relay user
fields.help: Sign in to the relay when set; the password belongs in the Vault ("{{ vault_mail_relay_password }}").

fields.name: mail_relay_password
fields.label: Relay password
fields.help: Kept in the Vault; on the server only root can read it.

columns.name: net_mode
columns.label: Address
columns.help: How the first network card gets its IPv4 address: static (ansible_host, net_prefix and net_gateway) or dhcp. With dhcp and no ansible_host, the address is read from the QEMU guest agent once the installed system boots and used as ansible_host for the rest of the run; the API token needs VM.GuestAgent.Audit (PVE 9) or VM.Monitor (PVE 8). With dhcp and an ansible_host (an address reserved for net_mac), that address is used.

columns.name: net_mac
columns.label: MAC address
columns.help: MAC address of net0, for example to reserve its DHCP address on the router. Empty uses one derived from the host name and VM ID, so a VM created again gets the same one.

columns.name: pve_vmid
columns.label: VM ID
columns.help: Required, fixed per host so reruns can find the VM.

columns.name: pve_node
columns.label: Node
columns.help: The Proxmox node of this server's VM; empty uses the node on the Proxmox page. Proxmox node name.

columns.name: vm_os
columns.label: OS
columns.help: Empty uses the default OS on the Defaults page. The server's operating system, from the OS catalog: ubuntu-26.04, debian-13, rocky-10 and so on (docs/interfaces.md lists them all). For all servers, or per server.

columns.name: vm_install_method
columns.label: Install method
columns.help: Empty uses the install method on the Defaults page.

columns.name: vm_extra_nics
columns.label: Extra network cards
columns.help: Comma-separated, each a bridge, then vlan and a tag, then dhcp, none or an address/prefix (optionally via a gateway), optionally mtu, model and mac. Example: vmbr1 vlan 20 10.20.0.5/24 mtu 9000, vmbr1 dhcp. More network cards (net1, net2, ...), each a mapping with these keys (only mode is needed for dhcp or none): The installed system matches each card by its MAC address. Example:.

columns.name: k8s_cluster
columns.label: Kubernetes cluster
columns.help: One of the clusters on the Defaults page; empty: not a member.

columns.name: k8s_role
columns.label: Kubernetes role
columns.help: server (the control plane and etcd) or agent (a worker); none: not a member.

kinds.apply: Install the updates (after a passing check)

fields.name: updates_scope
fields.label: What to install
fields.help: All: every update; security: only those from a security suite (Ubuntu's and Debian's -security pockets, ESM).

fields.name: updates_apt_upgrade
fields.label: How apt upgrades
fields.help: Safe: apt-get upgrade --with-new-pkgs (new kernels come in, nothing is removed). dist may remove packages, so it needs updates_scope: all and no updates_exclude_packages.

fields.name: updates_kernel
fields.label: Install kernel updates
fields.help: False leaves kernels alone (adds updates_kernel_packages to the excludes).

fields.name: updates_exclude_packages
fields.label: Packages to leave alone
fields.help: Shell globs of packages to leave alone in this run (never written to the server). An update that needs one of them skips the server, with the reason in the report.

fields.name: updates_reboot
fields.label: Reboots
fields.help: Never: report "reboot pending" only. if_required: reboot when the server asks for it, inside updates_reboot_window, then check its health.

fields.name: updates_restart_services
fields.label: Services that run old code
fields.help: Host: keep the server's own needrestart setting. list: only list the services to restart. auto: restart them.

fields.name: updates_health_services
fields.label: Services that must run after an update
fields.help: Health checks after an update or a reboot: services that ran before must run after, and these too.

fields.name: updates_snapshot
fields.label: Snapshot each VM before its update
fields.help: A Proxmox snapshot of each VM's disks before its update (not its memory), on the node it runs on now, through the API settings of the inventory (pve_api_host, pve_api_user, pve_api_token_id, pve_api_token_secret). The token's role needs VM.Snapshot (docs/updates.md, "Snapshots"); rolling back is left to a Proxmox admin.

fields.name: updates_snapshot_keep
fields.label: Snapshots each VM keeps
fields.help: How many of this playbook's snapshots each VM keeps after a healthy update (0 deletes the new one too), and the age in days after which they are deleted at the next run. Snapshots without the usas_upd_ name and the playbook's description (the operator's own) are never deleted.

fields.name: updates_serial
fields.label: Servers per wave
fields.help: Waves (tasks/plan.yml): the servers are updated a wave at a time, in inventory order, each in the first wave with room for it. A wave holds at most updates_serial servers (a number, or a percentage of the servers being updated), at most updates_group_max_parallel of each update group, and at most updates_node_max_parallel that may reboot (updates_reboot: if_required) on each Proxmox node; 0 means no limit for the last two. The run takes these three from the first server: set them for all servers (group_vars/all, or -e).

fields.name: updates_group_max_parallel
fields.label: Servers of an update group per wave

fields.name: updates_node_max_parallel
fields.label: Servers that may reboot per Proxmox node and wave

fields.name: updates_notify
fields.label: When to notify
fields.help: Notifications, sent once per run from the control node (set them for all servers, in group_vars/all): on-change (an apply updated or rebooted a server, a check found updates waiting, or a server failed or couldn't be reached), always, or only-on-error.

fields.name: updates_k8s_drain
fields.label: Drain Kubernetes members before a reboot
fields.help: Kubernetes members (in a k8s_<cluster>_servers or k8s_<cluster>_agents group, as for the k3s role): before a reboot the node is cordoned and drained (k3s kubectl drain --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data), from the server itself or, for an agent, from the cluster's first server in the inventory; once it's back, healthy and a Ready node again, it's uncordoned. A drain that doesn't finish in updates_k8s_drain_timeout seconds uncordons the node again and fails the server without a reboot. The waves never hold two servers of a cluster, nor a server with its agents. false reboots a member without draining it (its pods stop with it).

fields.name: updates_k8s_wait_longhorn
fields.label: Wait for Longhorn's volumes after each member
fields.help: After uncordoning a member, wait until every attached Longhorn volume is healthy again (its replicas rebuilt) before the server's update counts as done, so that the next wave starts with every volume whole; fails the server after updates_k8s_longhorn_timeout seconds.

fields.name: updates_k8s_ready_timeout
fields.label: Seconds to wait for a member to be Ready again
fields.help: Seconds to wait for the node to be Ready again after its reboot.

fields.name: updates_k8s_longhorn_timeout
fields.label: Seconds to wait for Longhorn's volumes

fields.name: name
fields.label: Name
fields.help: Lowercase letters, digits and -, starting with a letter: the groups are k8s_<name>_servers and k8s_<name>_agents.

fields.name: k8s_version
fields.label: k3s version
fields.help: The k3s release, one of the catalog's (roles/k3s/vars/catalog.yml): required. A member that already runs another release is refused, unless the run is an upgrade (--tags upgrade), which moves the cluster to this release one node at a time: servers first, then agents, forward only, one minor release at a time.

fields.name: k8s_api_vip
fields.label: API address (VIP)
fields.help: The API's address on the LAN, an IPv4 address no other host has: kube-vip holds it on one server at a time and moves it when that server stops. Empty: no kube-vip, and every member joins through the first server's address.

fields.name: k8s_lb_pool
fields.label: LoadBalancer pool
fields.help: The addresses LoadBalancer services get, from kube-vip's cloud provider: a range (192.0.2.20-192.0.2.29) or a network (192.0.2.32/28). Empty: none. Needs k8s_api_vip (kube-vip announces them) and servicelb in k8s_disable.

fields.name: k8s_api_sources
fields.label: API allowed from
fields.help: Who else may reach the Kubernetes API (6443/tcp) on the cluster's servers, besides its members: IPv4 addresses or networks (CIDR), or "any". Add the control node to run kubectl from it.

fields.name: k8s_server_taint
fields.label: Keep workloads off the servers
fields.help: Keep ordinary workloads off the servers (CriticalAddonsOnly=true:NoExecute). k3s' own add-ons still run there.

fields.name: k8s_flannel_backend
fields.label: Pod network between nodes
fields.help: The pod network between nodes, as the baseline's firewall rules expect (roles/kubernetes_node, same variable): vxlan or wireguard-native.

fields.name: k8s_longhorn_prereqs
fields.label: Longhorn's prerequisites
fields.help: Longhorn's node prerequisites: the iSCSI initiator (open-iscsi, or iscsi-initiator-utils on the RHEL family) with iscsid running, the NFS client, the iscsi_tcp module, and multipathd (where it's installed) told to leave sd* disks alone. Turning it off again removes the module and multipathd files, not the packages.

fields.name: k8s_disable
fields.label: Packaged components to leave out
fields.help: K3s' packaged components to leave out: servicelb, traefik, local-storage, metrics-server.

fields.name: k8s_api_vip_interface
fields.label: VIP network interface
fields.help: The network interface kube-vip puts the address on, the same name on every server. Empty: the first server's interface for its default route.

fields.name: k8s_tls_san
fields.label: More certificate names
fields.help: More names or addresses the API's certificate is valid for, besides k8s_api_vip (DNS names or IPv4 addresses).

fields.name: k8s_secrets_encryption
fields.label: Encrypt Secrets in etcd
fields.help: Encrypt Secrets in etcd. Turning it on or off in a running cluster takes k3s' own procedure (k3s secrets-encrypt), not just this setting.

fields.name: k8s_fetch_readonly_kubeconfig
fields.label: Fetch a read-only kubeconfig
fields.help: Kept in the data folder for kubectl from the container; the web UI never shows or offers it. Fetch a kubeconfig of a read-only ServiceAccount (bound to the view ClusterRole) to k8s_readonly_kubeconfig on the control node, mode 0600. The admin kubeconfig never leaves the servers.

fields.name: k8s_ready_timeout
fields.label: Seconds to wait for a node to be Ready
fields.help: Seconds to wait for a node to be Ready after k3s starts.

fields.name: k8s_drain_timeout
fields.label: Seconds a node's drain may take in an upgrade
fields.help: Seconds a node's drain may take during an upgrade (k3s kubectl drain --timeout). A pod that can't be evicted in time (a PodDisruptionBudget, a pod no controller manages) stops the upgrade with the node still cordoned.

fields.name: k8s_bootstrap_argocd
fields.label: Hand the cluster over to Argo CD
fields.help: The GitOps handoff (optional): once the cluster is Ready, Helm installs Argo CD's chart (both pinned in the catalog) on the cluster's first server, and one root Application makes Argo CD sync the rest from a Git repository (an "app of apps", like homelab-kube's bootstrap/root.yaml). That's where USAS stops: from then on Argo CD manages itself and the apps from Git, and a later run never upgrades, changes or syncs either of them. Argo CD's initial admin password stays in the argocd-initial-admin-secret Secret for the owner to read and delete (docs/interfaces.md).

fields.name: k8s_bootstrap_repo_url
fields.label: Git repository
fields.help: The Git repository the root Application syncs: an https:// URL with no user name, password, query or fragment. A private repository needs read access in Argo CD (Settings, Repositories) once it runs.

fields.name: k8s_bootstrap_path
fields.label: Folder of the Applications
fields.help: The folder in the repository with the Applications ("." for its top), and the branch, tag or commit to follow.

fields.name: k8s_bootstrap_revision
fields.label: Branch, tag or commit
fields.help: What the root Application follows in the repository.

fields.name: k8s_bootstrap_repo_ca
fields.label: The Git server's CA certificate (PEM)
fields.help: The certificate (PEM) of the CA that signed the Git server's certificate, if it isn't a public CA's: Argo CD trusts it for that server only. Empty: public CAs only.

fields.name: k8s_bootstrap_timeout
fields.label: Seconds Helm waits for Argo CD
fields.help: Seconds Helm waits for Argo CD's pods to be ready.

tokens.name: k8s_token
tokens.label: Server join token
tokens.help: Servers join with it. 32 to 128 letters and digits, such as openssl rand -hex 32 makes.

tokens.name: k8s_agent_token
tokens.label: Agent join token
tokens.help: Agents join with it, so a worker can't join as a server. Not the server token.
